_paper_icpsr_main.note: Paper Table 1 (ICPSR 22140 HIV network, 5 component-level folds, d=3, k=24, gamma=0.99, T=|V|), transcribed unchanged. The ICPSR data needs a signed user agreement, so the gym scores a synthetic referral-forest substitute instead; these numbers are on a different dataset and are kept for context only, not as values the gym must match.
_paper_icpsr_main.metrics_note: auc = area under the cumulative discounted reward curve; reward_X = cumulative discounted reward after X of the population is tested.

synthetic_main.description: Sequential HIV testing on incrementally revealed referral forests (synthetic substitute for the gated ICPSR network, at the paper's per-fold scale: ~155 people per test graph, ~11% HIV prevalence, gamma=0.99, budget T=|V|). Each method is played interactively on 120 held-out episodes generated inside eval/test/ (unreadable while policies run); it sees only roots, the people its tests reveal and the labels of people it tested. Any invalid action, crash or timeout fails the run (worst value in every metric).

auc.description: Area under the cumulative discounted positive-detection curve (mean over the T=|V| testing steps), averaged over held-out episodes weighted by people per episode.

reward_25pct.description: Cumulative discounted positive detections after 25% of each episode's population has been tested.

reward_50pct.description: Cumulative discounted positive detections after 50% of each episode's population has been tested.

reward_75pct.description: Cumulative discounted positive detections after 75% of each episode's population has been tested.

synthetic_main.notes: Results are the hidden-test scores of the final reference code (PEGE+DDB, k=24, d=3, mean aggregation, seed 11) and the paper's simple baselines, identical to scoring/scores_test.json. Scaled setup: synthetic data instead of ICPSR, so these values are not on the paper's scale; the paper's Table 1 is kept under _paper_icpsr_main. Coefficients follow the paper's emphasis on total AUC and the 25% budget (its headline '9% more detections with 25% tested').
